around.headline: Karnataka HC upholds transport department action in a Mercedes registration fraud case
around.summary: The Karnataka High Court has upheld the state transport department's action in a case involving fraudulent registration of a Mercedes-Benz in Bengaluru. If you're buying a used or premium vehicle, verify the registration certificate and ownership history directly with the RTO (via the Vahan portal) rather than trusting the seller's paperwork alone.

around.headline: 10 children rescued from a Bengaluru railway station this month
around.summary: Authorities have rescued 10 children from a Bengaluru railway station so far this month, a reminder of the runaway and trafficking risk around the city's transit hubs. If you spot a child alone and in distress at a station, alert the Railway Protection Force (139) or Childline (1098) instead of walking past.

around.headline: Goraguntepalya set for extra lanes, but jams may persist
around.summary: Authorities plan to widen lanes at Goraguntepalya, one of the city's worst traffic bottlenecks, though officials caution congestion may not ease right away. Commuters on the Tumkur Road–Outer Ring Road stretch should still budget extra time through this junction for now.

around.headline: HC revokes land acquisition for Bengaluru-Mysuru Infrastructure Corridor, calls it possibly the biggest scam
around.summary: The Karnataka High Court has revoked the land acquisition for the long-running Bengaluru-Mysuru Infrastructure Corridor, remarking it could be one of the biggest scams and that farmers were robbed of their land. The ruling stalls the project and is worth watching if your commute or property plans depend on that corridor.

around.headline: Price rise in bananas and eggs squeezes Karnataka's midday meal budgets
around.summary: Rising prices of everyday staples like bananas and eggs are straining budgets for Karnataka's school midday meal scheme. It's a sign the same grocery inflation pinching school kitchens is likely showing up in your own weekly shopping bill too.

around.headline: Lok Sabha passes Public Examinations Amendment Bill 2026, minimum 5-year jail for exam malpractice
around.summary: Parliament's Lok Sabha has passed the Public Examinations Amendment Bill 2026, setting a minimum 5-year jail term for exam paper leaks and malpractice, following this year's NEET leak controversy. If you have a student in the family prepping for competitive exams, this raises the legal deterrent against the kind of leaks that have disrupted recent exam cycles.

street_smart.title: Your landlord sends a WhatsApp message giving you 7 days to vacate because he wants to sell the flat — your rental agreement doesn't mention a notice period. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Evergreen rotation topic (tenant/landlord rights) — no single incident in today's feeds gave enough detail for a clean trap scenario (today's real Bengaluru stories were a court land-acquisition ruling, a vehicle registration fraud case, and a bus assault, none of which fit the format). Tenant/landlord rights hasn't appeared in the last 3 weeks of briefs — the last rental-related scenario, on deposit deductions, ran July 16.
street_smart.situation: You're renting in Bengaluru like a huge share of the city's workforce, and the message lands out of nowhere with a deadline that feels impossible to meet.

choices.text: Reply in writing (keep it on WhatsApp/email) pointing to your agreement's notice-period clause, and if it's silent, note that reasonable notice — typically at least a month, tied to your rent cycle — applies by standard practice, then propose a realistic move-out date.
choices.feedback: Correct. Your agreement's terms bind both sides, and 'silent' doesn't mean 'zero' — it defaults to reasonable notice tied to how rent is paid, usually monthly. Putting your position in writing also creates a paper trail if the landlord later tries pressure tactics like cutting utilities.

choices.text: Start packing immediately and plan to be out within 7 days, since it's his property and he can ask for it back whenever he wants.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Ownership doesn't erase your rights as a tenant during the agreed lease term — a landlord can't unilaterally shrink the notice period below what the agreement or standard practice allows just by asking. Complying without pushback trains landlords that pressure works, and rushed moves often mean lost deposits and bad next-place decisions.

choices.text: Don't reply at all — ignore the message and hope the landlord drops it or forgets.
choices.feedback: Silence doesn't protect you here — it can be read as ignoring a legitimate notice, and it wastes time you could spend negotiating a fair timeline in writing. A documented, reasonable response counts for far more than no response if this turns into a dispute.

choices.text: Call the landlord and verbally agree you'll be out in three weeks, without confirming it over text or email.
choices.feedback: Verbal agreements are hard to prove later. If the landlord denies what was said or tries to change the date again, you have nothing to point to — always get the agreed timeline confirmed in writing, even if it's just a follow-up message summarizing the call.

takeaways: Check your rental agreement's notice-period clause first; if it's silent, reasonable notice (commonly a month, matching the rent cycle) is the standard default in practice.
Always get agreements about vacating, timelines, or deposit conditions in writing (WhatsApp/email) — verbal promises don't hold up in a dispute.

A landlord cutting water, power, or access to pressure you out is illegal; you can report it to the local police station, and rent-related disputes can go to your area's rent court or a consumer forum.

quiz.q: Which chronic Bengaluru traffic bottleneck is set to get extra lanes, though officials warn jams may persist?
quiz.why: Goraguntepalya sits on the busy Tumkur Road–Outer Ring Road stretch, one of the city's most congested commute corridors.

quiz.q: The Karnataka High Court recently revoked land acquisition for which long-running project, remarking it could be one of the biggest scams?
quiz.why: The court's remarks centered on farmers whose land was acquired for the corridor, a project that has faced legal challenges for years.

quiz.q: The Public Examinations Amendment Bill 2026, passed by the Lok Sabha this week, sets what minimum jail term for exam paper leaks?
quiz.why: The bill follows this year's NEET leak controversy, which put a spotlight on gaps in exam-security law.

quiz.q: Which constitutional body is responsible for conducting elections to the Lok Sabha and state assemblies in India?
quiz.why: The Election Commission is an independent body set up under Article 324 of the Constitution, separate from the government of the day.

quiz.q: Which wind system brings most of Bengaluru's rainfall between June and September, the season we're still in?
quiz.why: The southwest monsoon dominates June–September rainfall across most of India; Bengaluru gets a second, smaller boost from the northeast monsoon later in the year.
